portability.title: Data transfer
portability.description: Pick account data or a single Bot. Imports are checked first and create copies. Account and Bot bundles share one format and are encrypted by default.
portability.scope_note: Supported now: configuration, chat text, memories, scheduled tasks, attachments, and timezone/language/model settings. Attachments are limited to 4 MiB each and 8 MiB in total; missing or oversized files are listed. You can also choose persistent vault environment credentials explicitly; only inactive copies are restored. SSH private keys, sign-ins, plugins, skills, work items, mail drafts, run history, virtual Bot computer files and whole disks aren't supported yet. This is a selected bundle, not a full account backup. Secrets pasted into chats or instructions are still exported with the text.
portability.security_note: The export passphrase stays in your browser. Anyone with the bundle and the passphrase can read it. Importing sends the decrypted bundle to the target server, and your selection decides which records are written. The server handles plain text: an account manager who resets a password can take over the account, and the host administrator can read run data. This isn't storage kept secret from the operator. The vault and the database are snapshotted separately.
portability.environment_note: Environment credentials are off by default, and each record must be checked individually. Up to 64 records, 64 KiB each, 1 MiB in total. This doesn't include environment variables installed on the Bot computer, SSH, or service sign-ins.
portability.dependency_note: Bot configurations and empty direct chats needed by history references are included as dependencies. Former group members aren't restored, and their other chat text isn't included.
portability.bot_note: A single-Bot bundle includes only that Bot's direct chats; group chats aren't exported.
portability.import_environment_note: Environment credentials are off by default. After selecting the category, check each record. Only inactive recovery copies are created; nothing with the same target is overwritten, and no service is connected or installed on the Bot computer.
portability.attachment_space: Attachment space: about {{size}} KiB, counted against the target account's file storage quota.
portability.database_space: Estimated database space: about {{size}} KiB. SQLite decides the actual size; if space runs out, the whole import rolls back.
portability.preview_note: Bots and all related records get new IDs; existing content is kept. Unselected content is skipped. Bot configurations needed by history references are kept as dependencies; former group members and other direct chat text aren't restored. Group chats need all their current members selected. The preview is valid for 15 minutes.

conversation_model.name: Conversation model
conversation_model.what: Runs chats, group work, scheduled runs and anything that uses tools. A Bot's own model setting overrides it.

background_model.name: Background model
background_model.what: Handles light work behind the scenes: history summaries, routing, reviews and follow-up checks. Automatic means Haiku with Claude, and the conversation model elsewhere.

structured_output.name: Structured replies
structured_output.what: Only a Bot's finished replies appear in the chat; what it writes while working stays in the activity view. Turn off to post everything as before.

force_say_haiku_dm.name: Reply tool required for Haiku
force_say_haiku_dm.what: In direct messages, Haiku must reply through the chat every turn, so its answer always lands in the conversation.

web_search.name: Web search
web_search.what: Claude models search the web on their own, and read the pages they rely on, before answering when a question may be newer than what they know.

web_fetch_limit.name: Pages read per run
web_fetch_limit.what: The most web pages a Bot may read in one run. Past it, the Bot works from the pages it has. Raise it for research that spans many pages.

group_exchange_gists.name: Finished group exchanges, summarized
group_exchange_gists.what: In group chats, exchanges that wrapped up without a Bot are folded into a short gist for it.

own_replies_verbatim.name: Own replies kept in full
own_replies_verbatim.what: A Bot sees this many of its latest replies word for word. Older ones shrink to a one-line gist so it stops copying its own phrasing.

completion_review.name: Completion review after tool work
completion_review.what: After using tools, a Bot checks its answer against the actual results once before it replies.

answer_gate.name: Review scheduled and background work before delivery
answer_gate.what: A reviewer reads each draft result of a scheduled run against a rubric before it is delivered, and a weak draft goes back to the Bot for another try. This is how many times a draft can be sent back; 0 turns the review off. Chat replies are never reviewed.

mcp_auto_review.name: Automatic review of tool calls
mcp_auto_review.what: A background reviewer looks at calls to outside tools. Observe only records advice; Auto lets low-risk calls go through on its say-so.

remembered_approval_hours.name: Remembered approvals last
remembered_approval_hours.what: When you choose Remember on an approval, the same call is allowed in that chat for this long.

provider_retries.name: Automatic retries
provider_retries.what: Temporary model errors, such as overload or a dropped connection, are retried this many times before a run fails. 0 turns retries off.

schedule_receipt_review.name: Check scheduled runs before they finish
schedule_receipt_review.what: A scheduled run that ends without a completion record gets one chance to finish the job before it is marked done.

desktop_idle_seconds.name: Desktop idle hibernation
desktop_idle_seconds.what: The Bot computer hibernates after this long unused and wakes on the next tool call. Set by the Bot computer service.

group_triage.name: Route unaddressed group messages
group_triage.what: When a group message names no one, a background model picks the member whose role fits it best. Off sends it to the Primary Assistant, or to a random member when there is none. A group with one active member skips the step.

group_triage_model.name: Group routing model
group_triage_model.what: The model that picks the member for an unaddressed group message. Automatic means the background model.

group_followup_to_working.name: Follow-up messages go to the member still working
group_followup_to_working.what: When a group message names no one and a member is still working on the person's previous message, the new message goes to that member as a queued note, read at its next step, instead of being routed again. Once that member has answered, the next message is routed as usual. Off routes every such message.

task_retention_days.name: Finished tasks kept for
task_retention_days.what: After this many days a finished task loses its request text, checklist and revisions. Its title and one-line result stay. 0 keeps everything.

command_check_minutes.name: Command check interval
command_check_minutes.what: When a Bot waits for a command to end, a timed check wakes it after this long in case the end signal is lost. A timer the Bot sets itself replaces it.

computer_idle_off_minutes.name: Cloud computer idle turn-off
computer_idle_off_minutes.what: An E2B computer that has done nothing for this many minutes turns off (pauses). Its files are kept, and it turns on when a Bot needs it. E2B bills while it runs.

browser_engine.name: Browser control
browser_engine.what: How a Bot works in the Bot computer's browser. Classic reads page text and clicks by visible text. Playwright reads an accessibility tree and acts on element refs, which is more exact on busy pages.

desktop_engine.name: Desktop control
desktop_engine.what: How a Bot works in desktop apps other than the browser. Classic uses screenshots and pixel clicks. Accessibility adds tools that read an app's element tree and act on element indexes, which is more exact in file managers and settings dialogs. The screenshot tool stays available.

personal_input_review.name: Review input on your Mac
personal_input_review.what: The reviewer checks input a Bot sends to your own paired Mac before it runs. Choose how much of that input it sees.

task_stall_rounds.name: Stall report after
task_stall_rounds.what: When a Bot that holds a task finishes this many rounds with no change in the task's checklist or status, the Bot at the root of the work is told once. The count starts again when the task moves.

task_tree_idle_message_limit.name: Idle messages per task tree
task_tree_idle_message_limit.what: How many messages the Bots of one piece of work may pass between them without progress. Progress is a checklist item that ends, a task that closes done, or a result handed in, and it restarts the count. At the limit they stop handing work to each other until progress happens, and the root Bot decides what to tell you.

task_fanout_width.name: Parts per delegation
task_fanout_width.what: How many parts a Bot may give in one call. A task tree also holds at most twice this number of open tasks at one time. A call over the limit is refused and the Bot joins parts or waits.

task_fanout_depth.name: Depth of divided work
task_fanout_depth.what: How many levels of tasks a piece of work may have below its root. 1 lets the Bot at the root give parts and nobody split them again; 2 lets a member split its own part once more. A member at the limit does its part or asks the Bot that gave it.

task_part_deadline_minutes.name: Part deadline
task_part_deadline_minutes.what: How long a part has when you are in the conversation and the Bot sets no time of its own. When it passes, the Bot that gave the part is woken with a timeout result and decides what to deliver.

task_part_deadline_scheduled_minutes.name: Part deadline in scheduled runs
task_part_deadline_scheduled_minutes.what: How long a part has when the work was started by a schedule and the Bot sets no time of its own. Nobody waits in the chat, so the default is longer.

widget_artifacts_auto.name: Open Artifacts when a Bot makes a file
widget_artifacts_auto.what: The first time a Bot hands over a file in a chat, the Artifacts widget opens beside the messages. Later files refresh its list. Off keeps it closed until you open it.

widget_computer_auto.name: Open the Bot computer when a Bot uses it
widget_computer_auto.what: When a Bot takes the Bot computer in the chat you are viewing, its widget opens beside the messages. It stays open and folds into a strip 30 seconds after the Bot lets go. Off keeps it closed until you open it.

settings_change_limit.name: Settings changes per run
settings_change_limit.what: The most settings changes a Bot may make by itself in one run. Past it, the Bot lists the rest for you to make. Only you change this number.

work_trace.name: Work trace
work_trace.what: Keeps small pictures of a Bot's screen work so you can review what it did. A page that may show a private input, and a private origin, are never kept. Off keeps no pictures at all.

trace_retention_days.name: Work trace kept for
trace_retention_days.what: How long the pictures of a Bot's screen work stay on the server. They are deleted after this period. Keep everything never deletes them.

trace_private_origins.name: Private origins
trace_private_origins.what: Sites whose pages never enter the work trace. One host or origin per line. A host also covers its subdomains. Sites where a Bot used a private password input are always left out.

monthly_spend_limit_usd.name: Monthly spend limit
monthly_spend_limit_usd.what: Refuses calls to billed models once this month's spend reaches the limit, and sends one notice at 80%. Whole dollars, 0 is off. Set on the Usage page.

webtools.title: Web search & fetch
webtools.description: Where your Bots look things up. Each list runs from the top and moves to the next source when one fails.
webtools.master_off_body: Turn on Web search in Behavior to let Bots search and read pages.
webtools.no_search_title: No search source is set up
webtools.no_search_body: Bots can't search the web yet. Add a key or an address below. Reading a page by address still works.
webtools.search_note: Tried from the top. The first source that answers serves the Bot.
webtools.fetch_note: Reads one page by address. The built-in fetch always goes first.

about.native: Used first when the model brings its own search. No key needed.
about.builtin: Reads the page from this server and turns it into text. No key needed.
about.tavily: Search API for agents. Needs an API key.
about.brave: Independent search index. Needs an API key.
about.searxng: Your own SearXNG instance. Needs its address and JSON output enabled.
about.firecrawl: Scrapes pages that block plain requests. Needs an API key.
about.brightdata: Unlocks heavily protected sites. Needs an API key and a Web Unlocker zone.
about.computer: Browses on the Bot computer when the other sources fail. Shown only when a Bot computer exists.

webtools.move_hint: Drag, or use the arrow keys
webtools.address_note: Your own address, so a private network address is fine. The instance must allow JSON output.
webtools.key_note: Stored sealed on this server. It is never shown again.

code.quota_exceeded: No credit left or rate limited

webtools.limits_note: Each paid source stops after this many calls in 24 hours, and the list moves to the free sources.

managed.search_provided: Provided by your organization. Sources and order are read-only.
managed.fetch_provided: Provided by your organization. Sources and order are read-only.
managed.fetch_builtin: Managed by policy. Bots use the built-in page reader only.
managed.search_off: Web search is turned off for this account by policy.

standing.tier_changed: This tool's setting changed. Asks again.

remembered.empty: Nothing is remembered in any chat.

how.read: Read-only tools the service marks, or you mark.
how.write: The default. Each call is reviewed: what you asked for runs, the rest asks you.
how.high: You decide every call. When no one is there to ask, the call does not run.

chats.server_unsupported: The server needs an update to send notifications

spend.title: Monthly limit
spend.description: Counts what API-key models and priced compatible models cost at list price over the calendar month, in your time zone. ChatGPT and Codex sign-ins, local models and unpriced models are not counted.
spend.limit_help: Off by default. At 80% you get one notice. At 100%, every billed model call is refused: new runs, the next call of a run already going, and background calls such as follow-up checks and reviews.
spend.plans_note: ChatGPT and Codex sign-ins have no per-call price, so plan limits apply and they are never counted or refused. Local models and compatible models without a known price are not counted.

state.reached: Limit reached. Calls to billed models are refused.

If it is not listed, drag the icon from the card below the window into it. macOS may ask you to reopen Tofi, and the first capture may prompt you to bypass the system private window picker. perm.monthly: After Screen Recording is on, macOS asks about once a month whether Tofi may bypass the system private window picker. Choose Allow to keep capturing. Only you can answer this prompt; a Bot that runs into it will tell you.
perm.stale: Tofi is already on in System Settings but still shows Not allowed here? That entry belongs to an earlier copy of Tofi. In System Settings, select Tofi, click − to remove it, then choose Open System Settings here and turn it on again.

bots.empty: No Bot has asked to use this Mac yet.

control.paused_takeover: Desktop control is paused (you took over the mouse or keyboard).

local.title: Local execution
local.description: Let this server's Bots run commands in one folder you pick.
local.serverNone: Shown once a folder is chosen

summary.unknown: Can't read the execution status. Commands are disabled.
summary.unbound: The authorization is not bound to this server. Choose the folder and authorize again.
summary.running: Authorized for this server · a command is running
summary.ready: Authorized for this server · no command running

reason.faulted: Process cleanup was not confirmed. Stop or revoke, then refresh.
reason.unavailable: Refresh the status and try again.

select.idle: Choosing a folder does not grant anything. You confirm the authorization separately.
select.pending: Not authorized yet. Check the folder and the target server, then authorize.
select.noApi: This version has no native authorization. Update the app and try again.
select.cancelled: Authorization cancelled. The chosen folder has no new access.
select.changed: The authorization changed. Choose the folder and confirm again.
select.unknown: Can't tell whether the choice is still valid. Refresh, then choose again.
select.authorized: Folder authorized for this server's Bots.
select.unconfirmed: The authorization could not be confirmed. Choose the folder and authorize again.
select.revoked: Authorization revoked. Choose a folder and authorize again to use it.
select.revokePending: Revocation is not confirmed. Try again and refresh the status.

local.boundary: Commands can read the authorized folder, tools in ~/.local/bin, and any file outside your home folder that you can read. They can write only inside the authorized folder and a private project workspace, and changes are not rolled back. Tools in ~/.local/bin are read-only but can change while authorized, and running them can have side effects. The rest of your home folder and credential folders cannot be read or written. There is no SSH, network or Keychain access yet. The private workspace stays in a local temporary folder after you revoke; it is not cleaned up automatically.
local.persist: The authorization survives leaving this page. It ends when you quit the app, switch servers or revoke it.

pair.note: Device credentials stay in the desktop app's main process and are never sent to the page.

error.noStatus: No execution status was returned. Refresh and try again.
error.invalidSelection: No valid folder and target server were returned. Choose again.
